headline: High-risk filesystem and network overlap: Open Interpreter can write/egress broadly while Pipecat can relay shared-bus conversation state to external services.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Open Interpreter can read/write the local filesystem and clipboard, while Pipecat runs on a shared bus and handles conversation state. That creates a plausible content-bridging path where attacker-controlled text from one side can be treated as instructions by the other. The interaction is inferred from documented surfaces, not directly reproduced.
conditions: IF Open Interpreter copies untrusted text into files or clipboard that Pipecat later consumes from the shared bus, injection is possible.
IF Pipecat forwards conversation state into downstream prompts without provenance filtering, attacker instructions can propagate.
mitigations: Disable clipboard-based handoff between the agents.
Add a provenance tag to all shared-bus messages.
Require a human review step before Pipecat consumes Open Interpreter output.
Restrict Open Interpreter to a dedicated workspace directory.
requires-engineering: implement content sanitization for any text passed between agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Open Interpreter can access the entire local filesystem at the user's privilege and has broad network egress; Pipecat touches text, audio, video, images, and conversation state and can call many third-party APIs. If they share a workspace or bus, sensitive local files can be surfaced into Pipecat flows and then transmitted externally. The blast radius includes exfiltration, so severity is high.
conditions: IF Open Interpreter reads secrets from the local filesystem and Pipecat ingests that content into its conversation state, leakage occurs.
IF Pipecat routes shared-bus text or media to any configured third-party STT/LLM/TTS service, local data can leave the machine.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate OS users.
Disable shared filesystem access to sensitive directories.
Route Pipecat only to local providers for test runs.
Rotate any secrets stored on the machine before pairing.
requires-engineering: add per-message data-class filtering before external API calls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Open Interpreter has filesystem write, shell, subprocess, and git-state modification; Pipecat supports shared-bus concurrency and multiple instances. If both are pointed at the same mutable workspace or repo, concurrent writes and git mutations can race and corrupt state. Because the profiles expose overlapping mutable surfaces, the conflict is dangerous by default when co-located.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or repository, file clobbering can occur.
IF Open Interpreter modifies git state while Pipecat or its wrappers also persist artifacts there, race conditions can corrupt commits or checkpoints.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate working directory.
Pause one agent before the other writes to shared artifacts.
Use a lock file around any git operation.
Mount the shared workspace read-only for Pipecat.
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination for shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Open Interpreter can generate code, shell actions, and filesystem changes, while Pipecat can carry conversation state across a shared bus. If Pipecat treats Open Interpreter output as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream responses or actions. The pathway exists in default-style integrations, but verification steps can interrupt it.
conditions: IF Pipecat forwards Open Interpreter output into a downstream agent without verification, incorrect facts can propagate.
IF Open Interpreter emits malformed code or commands that Pipecat reuses as text, the error can be amplified.
mitigations: Insert a verification step before Pipecat consumes Open Interpreter output.
Require citations or structured schemas for any factual claims.
Limit Open Interpreter output to summaries, not executable text.
Log and diff all handoffs between agents.
requires-engineering: enforce typed message contracts between the agents.

E_compliance.rationale: Open Interpreter touches anything reachable on the local machine and handles model-provider API keys, while Pipecat processes audio, video, images, text, and analytics/metrics and can send data to many external services. If regulated data such as EU PII or secrets enters the shared flow, retention and residency obligations can diverge across the pair. The profiles do not prove a specific regime, so this is a documented compliance-risk pathway rather than a confirmed violation.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is present in the local filesystem or conversation state, compliance obligations apply.
IF Pipecat is configured to send that data to a non-approved external provider, residency or retention mismatches can occur.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the shared workspace.
Disable analytics exports for sensitive runs.
Use only approved providers for any regulated workload.
Document retention settings for both agents.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for data-class and residency routing.
